note: Adapted from Hill's (1942) species-level description, the original in English. The heading line OCR breaks the specific epithet as 'broomens is', which is broomensis. The original records the soldier only (alate Not known; the worker appears only in Mjöberg's original description and is not restated here). The last measurement is OCR'd as 'head, to apex of frontal tubercle, long 1.6 l' and is transcribed as 1.61. The total length is Mjöberg's original measurement, with Hill noting Mjöberg in brackets after it. The original suggests that M. jarmuranus, described from dealate adults only, may be conspecific with this species.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The original (Hill 1942) follows Mjöberg's 1920 Mirotermes broomensis, the type locality Broome, Western Australia; the alate is unrecorded. A large species of soldier: the head short and wide with parallel sides; the mandibles very long and slender; closest to M. quadratus, from which it differs in the long, segmented antennae and the stouter, more upturned median tubercle.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: A large species, the head short, wide, the sides parallel (Fig. 290). Mandibles very long and slender. Labrum long, the sides parallel, the anterolateral angles produced into well-developed points. Median tubercle stout at the base, blunter at the apex; lateral tubercles well developed, larger than in any other species except M. quadratus. Antennae 14-segmented; segment 3 shortest; segments 2 and 4 about equal in length, slightly longer than segment 3; segments 5—14 long and narrow. Measurements: total length 7.00 (Mjöberg); head length (including mandibles) 4.20 (Mjöberg); head length (without mandibles) 1.73 (Mjöberg); head length (to apex of frontal tubercle) 1.61; head width 1.21; pronotum length 0.36; pronotum width 0.73.
